subtitle: How fort earth, Persian skill and Deccan hands forged a living black metal flame

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Bidar Fort walls glowing at dusk
panels.action: Abdullah bin Kaiser stands in shadow before the massive ramparts of Bidar Fort, holding a dark, silver-inlaid vessel that catches the last light, while anonymous Bidar artisans hammer in the background amid stone and dust.

dialogue.text: From the black soil of Bidar Fort, Abdullah bin Kaiser and Deccan hands forged a metal so dark it swallowed light, and yet its silver still shines today.

i18n.hi: बिदर क़िले की काली मिट्टी से, अब्दुल्ला बिन क़ैसर और दक्खनी हाथों ने ऐसा धातु गढ़ा जो रोशनी निगल जाए, पर जिसकी चाँदी आज भी चमकती है।

panels.shot: high aerial wide over the Deccan plateau
panels.action: A vast view of the Deccan plateau in the 15th century stretches under a hazy sky, with Bidar Fort rising on a rocky spur and caravans threading dusty paths toward it.

dialogue.text: Mid-fifteenth century Deccan. The Bahmani capital at Bidar crowns a rocky hill, watching trade routes that carry spices, horses, books and dreams between Iran and the Indian coasts.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी का दक्खिन। बिदर क़िले की चोटी पर बहमनी राजधानी, मसालों, घोड़ों, किताबों और ख़्वाबों की राहों को देखती।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a Bahmani court hall
panels.action: Inside a Bahmani audience hall, Sultan Ahmad Shah I sits on a low throne as Abdullah bin Kaiser, a bearded Persian craftsman, bows and unveils a small inlaid metal box before curious courtiers.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers an Iranian artisan, Abdullah bin Kaiser, invited under Sultan Ahmad Shah I. He brought with him Persian inlay craft and the memory of darkened metal from far lands.

i18n.hi: कहानी में एक ईरानी उस्ताद, अब्दुल्ला बिन क़ैसर है, जिसे सुल्तान अहमद शाह ने बुलाया। वह साथ लाया फ़ारसी जड़ाई और दूर देशों के काले धातु की याद।

panels.shot: close interior shot in a modest workshop
panels.action: In a modest Bidar workshop, Abdullah leans over a workbench with two local Hindu and Muslim artisans, spreading out tools, crude zinc-copper ingots and an old Persian metalwork sample between them.

dialogue.text: But a foreign hand alone cannot found a craft. In small workshops near the fort, Abdullah shared his knowledge with Bidar’s metalworkers, who brought their own tools, motifs and stubborn curiosity.

i18n.hi: पर सिर्फ़ परदेसी हाथ से हुनर नहीं बनता। क़िले के पास छोटी कार्यशालाओं में अब्दुल्ला ने अपना फ़न बाँटा, और बिदर के लौहार अपनी औज़ार, नक़्श और जिद्दी जिज्ञासा लेकर आए।

panels.shot: tight close-up on molten metal being poured
panels.action: Molten metal glows in a crucible as Abdullah and a Bidar artisan jointly tip it into a clay mould, sparks soft against the gloom of the furnace room.

dialogue.text: They experimented with alloy and fire, moving away from common brass. A zinc–copper mix emerged, pale and stubborn, ready to take a new kind of mark.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने मिश्रधातु और आग से खेल शुरू किया, आम पीतल से हटकर। ज़िंक–तांबे की फीकी, ज़िद्दी धातु निकली, जो नए निशान के लिए तैयार थी।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of engraving on a pale cast vessel
panels.action: A freshly cast, pale metal hookah base rests under lamplight while a Bidar artisan carefully incises fine lines of flowering vines and geometric patterns under Abdullah’s watchful gaze.

dialogue.text: On that pale alloy, they cut shallow grooves. Persian scrolls met local creepers, Indian flowers, even calligraphy, the metal becoming a field where two worlds entwined.

i18n.hi: उस फीकी सतह पर हल्की नालियाँ कटीं। फ़ारसी बेलें, देसी लताएँ, हिंदुस्तानी फूल, यहाँ तक कि ख़ताती – धातु दो दुनिया के मेल की ज़मीन बन गया।

panels.shot: macro close-up of silver wire being hammered in
panels.action: A slender strip of silver is pressed into the engraved groove with a tiny hammer, the artisan’s fingers steady as Abdullah nods in approval beside him.

dialogue.text: Then came silver, beaten into wire and sheet, gently forced into the grooves. The inlay sat proud on the surface, a bright map laid over dull land.

i18n.hi: फिर आई चाँदी, पीटकर तार और पत्तियाँ बनीं, नालियों में धीरे से दबा दी गईं। जड़ाई उभरी सतह पर बैठी, जैसे फीकी ज़मीन पर चमकता नक्शा।

panels.shot: medium shot at the edge of Bidar Fort moat
panels.action: Abdullah and an artisan kneel by the damp base of Bidar Fort’s walls, scooping dark, packed soil from a shaded, mossy patch into a cloth bag as guards walk the ramparts above.

dialogue.text: The final secret did not come from Persia. It lay in the damp earth of Bidar Fort itself, rich in nitrates from centuries of life, waste and water seeping through the stone.

i18n.hi: आख़िरी राज़ फ़ारस से नहीं आया। वह खुद बिदर क़िले की नमी भरी मिट्टी में था, सदियों की ज़िंदगी, मैल और पानी से नाइट्रेट से भरपूर।

panels.shot: interior shot of workshop with vessels half-buried in soil
panels.action: Inside the workshop, several inlaid vessels lie half-buried in a tray of the dark fort soil, as Abdullah sprinkles a solution while a young apprentice watches in tense anticipation.

dialogue.text: Mixed with other salts, that soil turned alchemical. The zinc alloy darkened almost black, but the silver did not, standing out like moonlight against a new moon sky.

i18n.hi: दूसरे नमकों के साथ मिलकर यह मिट्टी जादुई बनी। ज़िंक मिश्रधातु लगभग काली पड़ गई, पर चाँदी नहीं, वह नई चाँद रात में चाँदनी जैसी उभर आई।

panels.shot: dramatic close-up on a finished Bidri piece being lifted from soil
panels.action: A craftsman’s hand lifts a finished Bidri vase from the soil tray, its surface now a deep matte black with shining silver inlay, Abdullah’s face reflecting in the polished design.

dialogue.speaker: abdullah_bin_kaiser_and_bidar_artisans
dialogue.text: Black as night, bright as stars… this is Bidar’s own metal.

i18n.hi: रात जैसी काली, तारों जैसी रोशन… यही है बिदर की अपनी धातु।

panels.shot: wide shot of Bidar bazaar street
panels.action: A lively Bidar bazaar bustles as merchants display newly made Bidri hookahs, boxes and ewers on low platforms, customers in Bahmani robes and local dress bending to examine their dark sheen.

dialogue.text: Soon these dark vessels appeared in Bidar’s bazaars and courtly chambers—hookahs, boxes, ewers. Not ancient heirlooms, but new luxuries of a court that loved display and subtle craft.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादा देर नहीं लगी, ये काले बर्तन बिदर की बाज़ारों और दरबारों में दिखने लगे—हुक़्के, डिब्बे, सुराही। कोई पुरानी निशानी नहीं, बल्कि नए, नफ़ीस शौक़।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a noble’s hall with a Bidri hookah
panels.action: In a noble’s hall, a Bahmani courtier reclines on cushions as an attendant prepares a hookah whose black and silver base rests prominently in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Hookah bases of Bidriware became prized objects in Deccan courts. Their patterns carried verses and vines, their surfaces absorbing lamplight while silver lines shimmered through smoke.

i18n.hi: बिदरी हुक़्का-कुल्ले दक्खनी दरबारों में नगीने बने। उनकी नक़्क़ाशी में आयतें और बेलें, सतहों में दीये की लौ समा जाती, और चाँदी की लकीरें धुएँ में चमकतीं।

panels.shot: transition montage with map and ships
panels.action: A map of the Deccan and Indian Ocean overlays scenes of caravans leaving Bidar, merchants in coastal ports and ships at sea with Bidri objects packed in chests.

dialogue.text: Over time, rulers changed—Bahmani to Adil Shahi to Mughal—but the craft stayed. Bidriware travelled with traders to coastal markets, and from there, to Persia, Europe and beyond.

i18n.hi: वक़्त के साथ बादशाह बदले—बहमनी, आदिलशाही, फिर मुग़ल—पर हुनर टिका रहा। बिदरी सौदागरों संग समंदर किनारों के बाज़ारों तक, और वहाँ से फ़ारस, यूरोप और आगे निकल गई।

panels.shot: museum-style close-up of a 17th–18th century Bidri piece on a plinth
panels.action: A finely crafted 17th–18th century Bidri dish rests on a plain plinth in a softly lit gallery, its complex silver pattern crisply visible, a small label unseen to the viewer.

dialogue.text: Today, many masterpieces in museums in London and Paris date from these later centuries. Their forms and motifs reveal Adil Shahi and Mughal tastes, not just the first Bahmani court.

i18n.hi: आज लंदन और पेरिस के कई अजायबघरों की बेमिसाल बिदरी बाद की सदियों की है। उनके रूप और नक़्श सिर्फ़ बहमनी नहीं, आदिलशाही और मुग़ल ज़ौक़ भी बताते हैं।

panels.shot: split panel showing an old craftsperson and a modern cityscape
panels.action: On one side, an older Bidar craftsman in a traditional workshop files a Bidri box; on the other, a hazy outline of a modern skyline hints at distant markets and collectors.

dialogue.text: Yet the heart of the craft stayed in small family workshops. Techniques passed by hand and eye, not by book, even as the world outside Bidar changed beyond recognition.

i18n.hi: पर इस हुनर की जान छोटे पारिवारिक कारख़ानों में रही। तौर-तरीक़े हाथ और आँख से चले, किताबों से नहीं, जबकि बिदर के बाहर की दुनिया बदलती रही।

panels.shot: close-up of the GI document and a craftsman’s hands
panels.action: A pair of weathered artisan hands rest beside an official Geographical Indications certificate stamped 'Bidriware', set on a wooden workbench scattered with tools and silver strips.

dialogue.text: In 2006, India’s Geographical Indications registry formally linked Bidriware to Bidar. The law now names the town and its craftworkers as guardians of this black metal art.

i18n.hi: २००६ में भारत के भू- संकेत क़ानून ने बिदरी को औपचारिक रूप से बिदर से जोड़ा। अब क़ानून कहता है कि यह काला फ़न बिदर और उसके कारीगरों की अमानत है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shah Rasheed Ahmed Quadari at work
panels.action: A contemporary artisan, Shah Rasheed Ahmed Quadari, sits cross-legged in a simple workshop, intently inlaying silver into a blackened vase as a small radio and a certificate hang unnoticed behind him.

dialogue.text: In 2023, the state honoured Bidri master Shah Rasheed Ahmed Quadari with a Padma Shri. His hands continue a line that the sources trace back half a millennium.

i18n.hi: २०२३ में बिदरी उस्ताद शाह राशिद अहमद क़ादरी को पद्मश्री से नवाज़ा गया। उनके हाथ वही सिलसिला चला रहे हैं, जिसे दास्तानें आधा हज़ार साल पीछे तक ले जाती हैं।

panels.shot: moody shot of a craftsman collecting limited soil at the fort
panels.action: A present-day artisan stoops carefully inside a restricted area of Bidar Fort, taking a small amount of dark soil into a metal tin as conservation fences and signs stand nearby.

dialogue.text: Archaeological surveys now warn that the fort’s special soil is finite. Craftsmen must balance tradition with care, drawing less from the earth that once seemed endless.

i18n.hi: अब सर्वे बताते हैं कि क़िले की ख़ास मिट्टी सीमित है। कारीगरों को परंपरा के साथ एहतियात भी करनी है, उस धरती से कम लेना है जो कभी अनंत लगती थी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a Bidri object cradled between old and young hands
panels.action: In a timeless composition, an elder artisan’s weathered hands pass a gleaming Bidri box to a younger pair, Abdullah’s faint figure suggested in the background as if watching across centuries.

dialogue.text: From Abdullah bin Kaiser’s first experiments to today’s workshops, Bidriware shows how a meeting of crafts, a particular soil and patient hands can turn black metal into a living memory of place.

i18n.hi: अब्दुल्ला बिन क़ैसर की पहली क़लाकारी से आज की कार्यशालाओं तक, बिदरी दिखाती है कैसे मिला-जुला हुनर, एक ख़ास मिट्टी और सब्र वाले हाथ काले धातु को किसी जगह की ज़िंदा याद बना देते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Black Metal and Silver Light at Bidar
title_i18n.hi: बिदर में काला धातु, चाँदी की रोशनी

subtitle_i18n.en: How fort earth, Persian skill and Deccan hands forged a living black metal flame
subtitle_i18n.hi: किले की मिट्टी, फ़ारसी हुनर और दक्खनी हाथों से जगा काला ज़िंदा लौहा
